claims.explanation: Repaglinide is a meglitinide insulin secretagogue that closes ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels by binding the SUR1/KCNJ11 complex, and its selective anticancer activity likely reflects dependence of certain tumor cells on KATP channel activity or on the drug's additional targets such as PPARG and OATP-mediated uptake. The strongest pattern in the observed lines is enrichment of TP53 mutation and RAS/RTK pathway activation among sensitive lines, suggesting that cells with defective p53 and/or MAPK/PI3K-driven survival signaling are more vulnerable to repaglinide-induced metabolic/ionic stress. Conversely, NRAS-mutant melanoma and several KRAS-mutant gastrointestinal lines were relatively resistant, indicating that specific oncogenic contexts modulate sensitivity.

PPARG is an annotated repaglinide target and may mediate antiproliferative effects
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines appear among sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are enriched among selectively killed lines
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines are enriched among least affected lines
NRAS-mutant melanoma line IPC298 was among the least affected
OATP1B1 uptake transporter expression could increase intracellular repaglinide exposure
OATP2B1 is a drug influx transporter that may enhance repaglinide uptake
CYP2C8-mediated metabolism may inactivate repaglinide and reduce exposure
SF3B1-mutant kidney and lung lines appear among least affected lines
